verdict.rationale: FireHydrant's Runbooks are its documented automation engine. They attach to incidents, evaluate their conditions automatically when an incident is declared, and include steps such as creating a Slack channel, assigning a role and adding a task list. Running diagnostics is not documented directly; the closest evidence is a Send-a-Webhook step that can call internal systems (example given: rolling back deployments), so that part of the story is only implied. Missing for 10: an explicitly documented diagnostics-running runbook step, and independent or hands-on corroboration of automatic step execution.

support.subject: As an SRE, runbooks attach to incidents and their steps can trigger automatically — creating channels, assigning tasks, running diagnostics

citations.quote: Runbooks are FireHydrant's automation engine. They define and automate a workflow of steps and actions according to specified conditions.
FireHydrant builds a Default Runbook for you that always attaches to every incident.
Any time an incident is declared, Runbooks evaluate their conditions to decide whether or not they should trigger.
Some examples of actions include creating a Slack channel, starting a Zoom meeting
The default Runbook will always have two default steps: Assign a Role... Add Task List
If you have internal systems that perform tasks like rolling back deployments, you may want to dispatch an HTTP request from FireHydrant to those systems.
